title: Captured frames are written to the DB with NO gain, offset, sensor temperature, mount pointing, focuser position or target link - although the FITS file it just wrote has all of them
what_happened: Run 1 captured 4 lights. The FITS header on disk is complete: GAIN=100, OFFSET=10, CCD-TEMP=15.0, SET-TEMP=15.0, RA=0.0/DEC=0.0, OBJCTRA/OBJCTDEC, FOCUSPOS=25074, FOCTEMP=20.0, SITELAT=30.0, SITELONG=82.0, OBJECT='New Target'. The matching captured_images rows have gain=NULL, offset=NULL, sensor_temp=NULL, cooler_power=NULL, mount_ra=NULL, mount_dec=NULL, mount_altitude=NULL, mount_azimuth=NULL, pier_side=NULL, focuser_position=NULL, focuser_temp=NULL, rotator_angle=NULL and target_id=NULL. Only hfr, star_count, eccentricity, filter, exposure_duration and binning were persisted.
expected: Every value the capture pipeline already knows (it wrote them into the FITS header microseconds earlier) should land in captured_images. Everything downstream reads the DB, not the file: the dark library matches on gain/offset/temp/duration/binning, analytics plots temperature and HFR, project tracking counts frames per target.
repro: Run any sequence with Cool Camera + Take Exposures against the simulators, then: sqlite3 <profile>/data/skotiq.db 'select gain,offset,sensor_temp,mount_ra,focuser_position,target_id from captured_images;' and compare with the FITS header of the same file.
evidence: DB row 1: /tmp/ns-audit/r-sequencer-run/captures/New Target_nofilter_0001.fits -> gain,offset,sensor_temp,mount_ra,mount_dec,focuser_position,target_id all empty. FITS header of that same file: GAIN=100 OFFSET=10 CCD-TEMP=15.0 FOCUSPOS=25074 RA=0.0 DEC=0.0.
location_wrong: unit says 'screen:sequencer/sequencer_screen.dart'; the defect is packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/daos/images_dao.dart:657 (insertSequenceFrame) and its only production caller packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_executor/event_operations.dart:708. sequencer_screen.dart has nothing to do with capture persistence.
proposed_fix: Populate captured_images from the same metadata struct used to build the FITS header, in one place, so the two cannot diverge. Add a regression test asserting the DB row and the header agree field for field.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced from scratch. Sequence > New Target > Take Exposures 4x3s LIGHT (Filter empty, Gain/Offset left on profile defaults), run against the sims. FITS header of New Target_nofilter_0001.fits: GAIN=100, OFFSET=10, CCD-TEMP=20.0, XBINNING/YBINNING=1, SITELAT=30.0, SITELONG=82.0, RA=0.0, OBJCTRA='00 00 00.00', DEC=0.0, OBJCTDEC='+00 00 00.00', FOCUSPOS=25000, FOCTEMP=20.0, OBJECT='New Target'. The four matching captured_images rows: gain, offset, sensor_temp, cooler_power, mount_ra, mount_dec, mount_altitude, mount_azimuth, pier_side, focuser_position, focuser_temp, rotator_angle ALL NULL and target_id NULL, while hfr (2.48-2.53), star_count (39), eccentricity, filter, exposure_duration 3.0, bin_x and session_id were persisted - row-for-row as reported. Root cause splits in two, which matters for the fix: (a) sensor_temp, cooler_power, mount_*, pier_side, focuser_*, rotator_angle are not in insertSequenceFrame's INSERT column list at all, so that path can never write them; (b) gain/offset ARE passed but come from attribution.gain/offset (the ExposureNode's per-node override), not from what the camera actually used, so a node on profile defaults writes NULL while the FITS card says 100/10. target_id resolves from the sequence tree and stays NULL because an ad-hoc Target node has no `targets` row (that table is empty after the run) - the Session Report itself files the frames as 'Untargeted'. P1 stands: dark-library matching keys on gain/offset/temp/binning and analytics/project tracking read the DB, not the file.

title: Light frames are written with NO pointing at all - no RA/DEC/OBJCTRA/OBJECT card and NULL mount_ra/mount_dec - after a successful slew to explicit coordinates
what_happened: Run 4 slewed the mount to RA 17.0000h Dec +30.0000 ('Slewing mount sim_mount_1 to RA=17.0000h Dec=30.0000', Slew completed Success at 14:57:13) and then captured 4 lights at 14:58:02-14:58:14. The FITS headers of those frames contain SIMPLE/BITPIX/NAXIS/EXPTIME/DATE-OBS/IMAGETYP/GAIN/OFFSET/CCD-TEMP/SET-TEMP/XBINNING/YBINNING/SITELAT/SITELONG/FOCUSPOS/FOCTEMP/NS-SESID/NS-FIDX/NS-NPLN - and nothing else. There is no RA, DEC, OBJCTRA, OBJCTDEC, OBJECT or FILTER card. captured_images.mount_ra / mount_dec / target_id are NULL for the same four rows. So after the run there is no record anywhere of where the telescope was pointed. (Frames taken under a Target node in run 1 did get RA/DEC cards, so the writer only emits pointing when a Target group exists, not when the mount is simply on target.)
expected: Every light frame carries the mount's actual RA/DEC at exposure start, regardless of whether the coordinates came from a Target group or from a Slew node's custom coordinates. This is basic FITS hygiene: stacking software, plate-solve verification and the app's own project tracking all key off it, and a sequence built around Slew-with-custom-coordinates (the flow the app itself pushes you to when it warns 'No target group found in sequence') silently produces unlabelled data.
repro: Builder: Cool Camera, Unpark, Slew to Target with Use Target Coordinates OFF and RA 17.0 / Dec 30.0, Autofocus, Take Exposures 4x3s, Park, Warm. Run to completion. Then dump the FITS header of any captured frame and select mount_ra,mount_dec from captured_images.
evidence: Header dump of /tmp/ns-audit/r-sequencer-run/captures/untargeted_nofilter_0001.fits (23 cards, no RA/DEC/OBJECT); sqlite 'select mount_ra,mount_dec,target_id from captured_images where producing_run_id=4' -> all NULL; app.log 14:57:12 'Slewing to RA: 17.0000h, Dec: 30.0000'
location_wrong: unit 'seq-node:ExposureNode' is approximately right for the FITS half (the header is assembled on the Rust capture path from the sequence context); the DB half belongs to images_dao.dart insertSequenceFrame + event_operations.dart, not the node.
proposed_fix: Read the mount's current RA/DEC from the device at exposure start and always write RA/DEC (plus OBJCTRA/OBJCTDEC) and persist them; fall back to the target group only for the OBJECT name.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end. Sequence with NO Target group: Slew to Target with 'Use Target Coordinates' OFF and RA 17.0000h / Dec 30.0000, then Take Exposures 4x3s LIGHT. Log: 'Slewing to RA: 17.0000h, Dec: 30.0000', 'Slewing mount sim_mount_1 to RA=17.0000h Dec=30.0000', then Child 'Slew to Target' completed with status: Success before the exposures. The four files (untargeted_nofilter_0001..0004.fits) have exactly 22 cards: SIMPLE, BITPIX, NAXIS, NAXIS1/2, BZERO, BSCALE, EXPTIME, DATE-OBS, IMAGETYP, GAIN, OFFSET, CCD-TEMP, XBINNING, YBINNING, SITELAT, SITELONG, FOCUSPOS, FOCTEMP, NS-SESID, NS-FIDX, NS-NPLN - no RA, DEC, OBJCTRA, OBJCTDEC, OBJECT or FILTER. captured_images rows 5-8 (producing_run_id=2): mount_ra, mount_dec, target_id all NULL. Control: the earlier Target-group run in the same app instance DID emit RA/OBJCTRA/DEC/OBJCTDEC/OBJECT, confirming pointing is emitted only when a Target group exists. One correction that matters for the fix: even in the working case the RA/DEC written are the TARGET's coordinates (0.0/0.0 for an unedited 'New Target'), not the mount's reported position - the writer never reads mount pointing at all, so 'every light frame carries the mount's actual RA/DEC' is not satisfied by either path. P1 stands: a night shot via Slew-with-custom-coordinates leaves no pointing record on disk or in the DB.
